# `project_workload` — version 2.0

Source: `presets/project-workload.satz`

## Purpose

Delegated access to projects: the Google projects teams work in from estates of their own,
and the account each is worked as. The account holds its roles on that project alone.
A project is a Google project this estate creates; the team's own estate, in its own
repository, fills it. Two lists, for two kinds of team.

A PROJECT WITH ITS OWN ACCOUNT. One entry of `project_workload_projects`,
{ name = "payments" owner_group = "payments-owners@example.com" }
is one Google project `{customer_shortname}-<name>-001` and, inside it, the service
account `svc-iac-<name>` its estate runs as and the state bucket
`{customer_shortname}-<name>-001-state`. The owner group reads the project and may
become that account — that account only.

A PROJECT WORKED BY A WORKLOAD'S ACCOUNT. One entry of
`project_workload_shared_projects`,
{ name = "shop-backend"  workload = "shop" }
{ name = "shop-frontend" workload = "shop" }
is one Google project and no account: the account of the workload `shop`, which
`presets/folder-workload.satz` declares (an entry of `folder_workloads`, with or
without folders of its own), gets the roles on it. One account then works in several
projects. The grant names the account by reference, so an entry that names a workload
no entry declares is refused by the compile, which lists the accounts that exist.

WHAT AN ACCOUNT HOLDS ON ITS PROJECT. `project_workload_roles` — the project's IAM
and its services — on that project and nowhere else: it creates no project and reaches
none beside its own. What its estate's resource types need beyond that it grants its
own account in its estate, on the project (`google_project_iam_member`, which the
interface allows).

BOTH KINDS. The project is billed to the infrastructure billing account and created in
`project_workload_folder`: empty is the organisation; the workload folder `satz init
--workload-folder-name` writes is `google_folder.workload_folder.name`. Its `apis` are
the five below unless the entry states its own list, whole. A `name` is the interface's
name and a folder name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter; a
group is the group's address, `<name>@<domain>`. Both lists are bound in the estate, or
requested by the team as `contributes_project_workload_projects` /
`contributes_project_workload_shared_projects` in a small pack of its own, checked with
`satz check-request` and vendored by pull request.

WHAT A PROJECT'S ESTATE READS. `interface "<name>"` publishes `project_id` (an attach
point for `google_project_iam_member`), `project_number`, and `delegated_project_roles`,
which `satz` judges the estate's needs against. A project with its own account
publishes `iac_account`, `state_bucket` and `delegated_apis` there too, and `satz init
--project <name> --interface interfaces/<name>/<name>/satz/interface.satz` writes its
estate from them. A project worked by a workload's account reads those from the
interface `workload-<workload>` of `presets/folder-workload.satz`, and uses both files.

MORE IN AN INTERFACE. An interface declared in two files is one interface, so the estate
adds to a project's interface by writing a block of the same name in its own file:
`interface "payments" { use interface "network" }`.

NO CLAIM. The projects are workloads, not controls: this pack witnesses nothing.

## Use it

```
params {
  use_project_workload = true

  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  project_workload_projects = []
  project_workload_shared_projects = []
  project_workload_folder = ""
  project_workload_roles = [
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin",
    "roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin",
  ]
}

use "presets/project-workload.satz" when use_project_workload
```

`use_project_workload` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `estate_map`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `billing_account_infra` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `default_region` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_workload_folder` | The folder the projects are created in — the workload folder as `google_folder.workload_folder.name`, another folder the estate declares as `google_folder.<label>.name`, an existing one by its numeric id, or empty for the organisation | edit | low | — |

**project_workload_folder** — It decides the policies and the grants every project inherits. Changing it afterwards moves every live project between parents.


## Contributes

| resource type | labels |
|---|---|
| `google_project` | `one per entry of project_workload_projects, by name`, `one per entry of project_workload_shared_projects, by name` |
| `google_project_iam_member` | `one per entry of project_workload_shared_projects, by name` |

## Exports

Outputs of the root module and values of the interfaces under `interfaces/` in every estate that uses this pack: a `core` export is carried by every interface, another one by its own interface and every interface that uses it. An interface a pack declares is common: every project's folder carries it.

| interface | output | value | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{each.name}` | `project_id` | `"${google_project.{each.name}.project_id}"` | The project's Google project — attach point for `google_project_iam_member` |
| `{each.name}` | `project_number` | `"${google_project.{each.name}.number}"` | Its number, looked up |
| `{each.name}` | `iac_account` | `"${google_service_account.{each.name}_iac.email}"` | The service account the project's estate runs as |
| `{each.name}` | `state_bucket` | `"${google_storage_bucket.{each.name}_state.name}"` | The bucket the project's estate keeps its state in |
| `{each.name}` | `account_group` | `"{each.owner_group}"` | The group whose members may act as the account |
| `{each.name}` | `account_group_roles` | `[ "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator", "roles/iam.serviceAccountUser" ]` | What that group holds on the account |
| `{each.name}` | `delegated_project_roles` | `project_workload_roles` | The roles the account holds on the project |
| `{each.name}` | `delegated_apis` | `each.apis` | The APIs enabled on the project, which the estate's calls are billed to |
| `{each.name}` | `project_id` | `"${google_project.{each.name}.project_id}"` | The project's Google project — attach point for `google_project_iam_member` |
| `{each.name}` | `project_number` | `"${google_project.{each.name}.number}"` | Its number, looked up |
| `{each.name}` | `delegated_project_roles` | `project_workload_roles` | The roles the workload's account holds on the project |

`{each.name}` is written once per entry of `project_workload_projects`, named by the entry's `name`, and each is one project's own interface, not a common one.

`{each.name}` is written once per entry of `project_workload_shared_projects`, named by the entry's `name`, and each is one project's own interface, not a common one.

## Requests

What a project may add to this pack's lists, through `contributes_<param>` in a file the estate uses after a reviewed pull request; `satz check-request` checks such a file.

| list | key | fields | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_workload_projects` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `owner_group` matching `[^@: ]+@[^@: ]+`, `apis` | A project with its own account: its name, which is its interface's, the address of the group that owns it, and the APIs enabled on it |
| `project_workload_shared_projects` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `workload` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `apis` | A project a workload's account works in: its name, which is its interface's, the workload of `presets/folder-workload.satz` whose account works in it, and the APIs enabled on it |
